items.title: Body believed to be missing five-year-old girl has been found in Alice Springs
items.description: NT Police say they have found a body believed to be that of a missing five-year-old Alice Springs girl.

items.title: 'None of it strikes me as nefarious': Judge queries ACCC case against Woolies
items.description: There have been tense exchanges in the Federal Court, with the judge overseeing the bombshell case between the ACCC and Woolworths questioning the consumer watchdog's case.

items.title: Chalmers does little to quell CGT debate as budget looms
items.description: Seven years ago, proposed changes to capital gains tax and negative gearing were named as part of the reason Labor lost the unlosable election. Times have changed.

items.title: Police told 'not to stay the entire duration' of Hannukah event before terror attack
items.description: NSW Police officers assigned to patrol the Hanukkah celebration targeted in the Bondi Beach terrorist attack were told they did not need to "stay the entire duration" of the event, despite members of the Jewish community fearing it was at risk.

items.title: Global Sumud Flotilla carrying Australians intercepted on its way to Gaza by IDF
items.description: The Global Sumud Flotilla has been intercepted by the IDF, an official tweet by the group says.

items.title: Apologetic insurer claims customers were not tricked in renewal notices
items.description: When the corporate regulator accused RACQ of misleading customers with insurance renewal notices it apologised. Now, it is defending the earlier notices in court filings.

items.title: Rebel Wilson trial told of 'culturally inappropriate Indian outfit' post
items.description: Rebel Wilson tells a court several social media posts targeting the lead actor on her film The Deb are all true, on her final day of cross-examination in a defamation trial.

items.title: Private school denies discouraging parents from telling victims about deepfake incident
items.description: The principal of a Tasmanian private school denies claims by two parents that the school ever tried to discourage them from telling their daughters they had been identified in AI deepfake images.

items.title: Blues out to rewrite State of Origin history in Newcastle series opener
items.description: The Blues are yet to enjoy success in Newcastle, a fact they are mindful of ahead of the first Women's State of Origin match against the Maroons.

items.title: 'Forever changed': Parents speak after children killed in house fire
items.description: A statement shared by the parents of two children killed in a Bowen Mountain house fire say their "family's world has been forever changed".

items.title: Mining prohibited 'in perpetuity' from culturally significant reserve
items.description: Pilungah Reserve, south-west of Mount Isa, has become Queensland's third special wildlife reserve, barring any future mining activity.

items.title: Artist who taught himself to paint after seeing Roy and HG portrait wins prize
items.description: Sean Layh has won the $3,000 Packing Room Prize at this year's Archibald Prize for his portrait of Jacob Collins, titled The tragicall historie of Hamlet, Prince of Denmarke.

items.title: Bottle shops awash with illicit booze as police probe arson attacks
items.description: The National Drug Research Institute found 30 per cent of bottle shops it audited across different areas of Melbourne and regional Victoria were stocking illicit alcohol.

items.title: SA premier defends course development despite LIV Golf doubts
items.description: Peter Malinauskas compares spending $45 million to redevelop the North Adelaide golf course to similar funding for the AFL to play in the Barossa Valley, as media reports suggest Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund is preparing to pull financial support for LIV Golf.

items.title: 20 years after the original, The Devil Wears Prada 2 has something to say
items.description: The Devil Wears Prada 2 drops the beloved (or loathed) characters from 20 years ago into a very different media environment.

items.title: The 'Jessica' tantrum trend explained
items.description: Whether it's at home or in the middle of a shopping centre, tantrums can test the patience of any parent or caregiver.

items.title: Why the latest inflation data matters to you
items.description: The latest inflation data is making headlines. Find out what it means for you in three minutes.

items.title: Fed-up residents 'leaving town' due to murky tap water
items.description: When residents of Narrandera, in southern NSW, turn on the tap, the water that comes out is sometimes so dirty it stains their clothes.

items.title: On-duty paramedic stabbed outside cafe in Melbourne's north
items.description: Police have arrested a man who allegedly stabbed an on-duty paramedic in the suburb of Reservoir, in Melbourne's north, before fleeing the scene.

items.title: Melbourne teacher charged after camera found in school bathroom
items.description: The 33-year-old was arrested at the school in the city's south-east after the discovery of a camera in a bathroom.

items.title: 'Unfathomable': Truckies want higher penalties for dangerous driving
items.description: Truck drivers say the fines for dangerous overtaking should match drink driving penalties due to the risk it poses to other road users

items.title: Man on trial over alleged cocaine smuggling into Port of Newcastle
items.description: Queensland man James Lake-Kusviandy Blee is on trial over a cocaine shipment into Newcastle.

items.title: Police charge man for allegedly attending businesses while nude
items.description: A Mount Gambier man is granted bail after he was allegedly nude while in businesses and on a busy main road three times in the past week.

items.title: Lyon clarifies resignation offer over comment to First Nations players
items.description: St Kilda coach Ross Lyon is proud of the way the club reacted after he offended a group of the club's First Nations players.

items.title: From cereal to clothing, see how the price of everyday items has changed
items.description: If it feels like everything is getting more expensive, that's because it is. With the rate of inflation rising this week, we've tracked how the price of everyday items has increased.
